concepts.def: Numerical data via surveys, experiments, statistics; favoured by positivists for generalisation.
Rich descriptive data via interviews, ethnography, content analysis; favoured by interpretivists.
Immersive fieldwork in community; Malinowski 'Argonauts of the Western Pacific' 1922 founding study.
Selection of subset to represent population; random, stratified, snowball, convenience.
Researcher's awareness of own influence on data; Bourdieu's reflexive sociology 1980s.

Anthropological Practice (Methods & Ethics) — a core area of Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Anthropological Practice (Methods & Ethics) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.
